To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the integration of adenocarcinoma type 2 ( Ad 2 ) DNA into host DNA in a transformed hamster cell line occurs via a short sequence homology between the viral and host DNA.
(1) the integration site of the adenovirus genome in hamster cells is determined by a short nucleotide patch, and (2) patch homologies are common between the adenovirus DNA and the cellular DNA.

the site of the integration of adenocarvirus DNA in mammaliam cells can be cloned and sequenced and that the unoccupied cellular DNA adjacent to the viral DNA has a sequence that is identical to that in the cellular DNA in the junction DNA fragment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the integration of foreign (viral or plasmid) DNA into mammalian cell genomes.
the integration of adenoid virus DNA in hamster cells.
the integration of viral DNA in mammalian chromosomes, and the mechanisms of viral DNA replication and expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the insertion of foreign DNA into the host DNA is a non‐specific, random event.
the integration of viral DNA into cellular DNA can be accomplished via short sequence homology, which may be a common feature of all DNA‐DNA integration processes.
the site of integration of Ad2 DNA in HE5 is determined by short homologies between the viral and cellular DNAs, and that these homologies can occur at many different sites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the integration of Ad2 DNA into the hamster genome was a random process, and that the site of the viral DNA‐cell DNA junction was determined solely by the sequence of the cellular DNA at the site of integration.
the integration site of the viral DNA in the host cell is determined by a short sequence homology between the right termini of the virus and the cellular DNA.
the integration of adenocarcinoma DNA in HE5 cells is not a unique event.
The main takeaway from our work is that
short nucleotide homologues can be used to integrate DNA in the host genome.
the cellular DNA sequence at the integration site is not unique, and that integration of the viral DNA can be mediated by short sequence homologies.
short homologies can occur at random in cellular DNA and that they are not restricted to the junction site.
